names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 7 Δεκεμβρίου, «Άγιος Αθηνόδωρος», with the rank word left off.

Read out of the name link behind days.pravoslavie.ru’s line for 7 декабря ст. ст., «Афинодор Месопотамский, прмч.», with the rank word left off. The line on the day page itself gives the name in the genitive and no country at all.

death.note: The year the day line closes with for 7 декабря ст. ст., «(ок. 304)», where «ок.» is the calendar's own hedge and is kept as «about». It falls inside the reign this folder already held as a floruit, which is why that reading stands beside it unchanged. Read 13 October 2026.

floruit.note: saint.gr: «καταγόταν από τη Μεσοποταμία και έζησε την εποχή του αυτοκράτορα Διοκλητιανού (290 μ.Χ.)». The page's parenthesis is a year inside the reign rather than a dated event, so the interval here is the reign and the page's own words are kept.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 7 декабря ст. ст. — «Мч. Афинодора (ок. 304).»

attestations.note: The same man and the same menologion day: the Greek entry this folder was made from places him in Mesopotamia in the time of Diocletian, and this calendar's name link and life page call him «Афинодор Месопотамский» and put him in Syrian Mesopotamia. `types` UNTOUCHED: the day line gives «Мч.», the martyr the folder already holds, while the name link gives «прмч.», a venerable-martyr, on the strength of the monastic life his life page says he led from his youth; the day line is what this row quotes and the discrepancy is recorded in the life.
Not checked: doxologia.ro's calendar for the same civil day (2 October 2026).

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 7ης Δεκεμβρίου — «Άγιος Αθηνόδωρος»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 7 Δεκεμβρίου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. The corpus already keeps an `athenodorus` with a venerated Greek row on 7 November, the companion of Gregory the Wonderworker of Neocaesarea; that is another entry on the same calendar and therefore another commemoration, the man here is of Mesopotamia and under Diocletian, and nothing on either page joins them. The site's gloss under the name — sculptors, a citharode, two Stoics — is its standing note on the name and not on the saint. No hymn is printed. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence.
Not checked: the Ohrid Prologue as printed by pravoslavno.rs (2 October 2026).
